title: Ethiopian Tomato Salad — Classic
community: All of Ethiopia — the classic tomato and jalapeño table salad
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Classic Tomato Salad — very ripe tomatoes diced with onion, green jalapeño, and coriander, dressed with lemon and oil. This extended version includes roasted green pepper and a touch of cumin for depth beyond the simpler ETH119.
longDesc: The classic tomato salad (distinct from the simpler ETH119) adds roasted green pepper and cumin — two elements that lift it from a fresh salad to something with more cooked depth. The roasted pepper skin adds a charred note.
ingredients: 1 green pepper — roasted, peeled, finely diced
½ red onion — very finely diced
equipment: Open flame or grill for pepper
steps: Roast green pepper directly over gas flame or under grill until charred all over.
Place in a sealed bag 5 minutes. Peel, deseed, and finely dice.
Combine tomatoes, roasted pepper, onion, and jalapeño.
Dress with lemon, oil, cumin, and salt.
chefTips: The roasted pepper is the upgrading element — the charred note adds depth.
Rest 5 minutes — salt draws out the tomato juices.
commonMistakes: Skipping the roasted pepper — the simpler version is ETH119.
cookingScience: Roasting the green pepper triggers Maillard reactions on its skin and partially caramelises its sugars — producing complex flavour compounds (pyrazines, furans) that add a smoky, complex note absent from raw peppers.
servedWith: Alongside all grilled and fried dishes
healthBenefits: Roasted pepper — higher beta-carotene bioavailability when cooked.
culturalNote: The classic Ethiopian tomato salad with roasted pepper is the marker of a cook who goes further — who takes the time to roast the pepper rather than adding it raw. It is attention to detail expressed as food.
